decisionMemo.businessProblem: A mid-cap aerospace & defense contractor with $2.1B revenue has seen EBITDA margin compress 200 basis points in one year (10.0% to 8.0%, EBITDA $204M to $168M) despite revenue growth and a strong $5.6B backlog (2.7x revenue, book-to-bill 1.1). Input costs have surged: materials +12% (to $735M, 35% of revenue) and labor +8% (to $546M, 26% of revenue). The structural issue is that approximately 70% of revenue ($1,470M) is concentrated in firm-fixed-price multi-year government and prime contracts that were priced before the inflation surge and that lack economic price adjustment (EPA) clauses. On this book, input-cost inflation cannot be passed through, while only the ~30% cost-plus/escalating book ($630M) recovers cost increases. Demand is strong and the backlog is full, so this is not a demand, volume, or market-share problem, and operational efficiency is not the identified gap. The central question is whether the margin decline is a structural pricing/contracting problem, a unit-economics/operations problem, or an operational bottleneck. The CEO must decide, within ~120 days, how to price next-cycle FFP bids and whether to file Requests for Equitable Adjustment (REAs) on existing contracts before the re-pricing window closes and before bidding additional FFP work that could lock in further underpriced backlog.

scenarios.name: Aggressive Recovery (Best Case)
scenarios.description: Execute all interventions in optimal sequence with full team commitment
assumptions: Team capacity fully available (no other initiatives)
Client budget approved for all recommended interventions
No external market shocks during implementation
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Revenue recovery within 90 days, competitive positioning restored
risks: Cascading failures if one intervention stumbles

scenarios.name: Staged Implementation (Recommended)
scenarios.description: Execute top 3 prioritized interventions sequentially, measure, then decide on next wave
assumptions: Top 3 interventions address critical path to revenue recovery
Team capacity for 1-2 major initiatives at a time
Monthly review gates to assess progress and adjust
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Measurable improvement in 60 days, foundation for growth set
risks: Slower overall recovery than aggressive path
Competitors may advance while we execute gradually
